name: Wonderful Tree!
description: God's Blessing on This ArrayForces! A Random Pebble You are given a tree with $$$n$$$ vertices, rooted at vertex $$$1$$$. The $$$i$$$-th vertex has an integer $$$a_i$$$ written on it. Let $$$L$$$ be the set of all direct children$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ of $$$v$$$. A tree is called wonderful , if for all vertices $$$v$$$ where $$$L$$$ is not empty, $$$$$$a_v \le \sum_{u \in L}{a_u}.$$$$$$ In one operation, you choose any vertex $$$v$$$ and increase $$$a_v$$$ by $$$1$$$. Find the minimum number of operations needed to make the given tree wonderful ! $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ Vertex $$$u$$$ is called a direct child of vertex $$$v$$$ if: $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ are connected by an edge, and $$$v$$$ is on the (unique) path from $$$u$$$ to the root of the tree.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line of input contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 1000$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 5000$$$) — the number of vertices in the tree. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the values initially written on the vertices. The third line of each test case contains $$$n - 1$$$ integers $$$p_2, p_3 , \ldots, p_n$$$ ($$$1 \le p_i \lt i$$$), indicating that there is an edge from vertex $$$p_i$$$ to vertex $$$i$$$. It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5000$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum number of operations needed to make the tree wonderful .
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1987E — Wonderful Tree! [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
